items.gist: Health and Family Welfare Minister U T Khader told district-level Teachers' Day celebrations in Mangaluru on Saturday that teachers must continuously update their knowledge and skills to keep pace with AI and modern technology, and stressed value-based education amid rising corruption and communalism. items.headline: NITK introduces new 'bold and balanced' engineering curriculum
items.gist: National Institute of Technology Karnataka, Surathkal, has implemented a new "bold and balanced" engineering curriculum from the BTech batch of 2026, reducing total credits while allowing Honours, minor or interdisciplinary degrees and balancing theory with practical work including labs, life-skills activities, industry internship, R&D projects and startup planning. Dean (Academic Programs) Professor Annappa said the three-year curriculum was developed with industry and alumni input, and Director Prof B Ravi said the institute aims to prepare students for the AI era by emphasising creativity, empathy, ethics and judgement alongside technical knowledge.

items.gist: Sri Krishna Janmashtami and Laksha Tulasi Archane celebrations were held with religious fervour at Sri Gopalakrishna Temple in Shaktinagar on Friday and Saturday, beginning with Panchamritha Abhisheka, Ganapati Homa and Mahapooja and including bhajana, a Harikatha Satsanga titled Bhakta Sudhama, and midnight Arghya Pradhana. items.headline: Vande Bharat runtime trial held between Yeshwantpur, Mangaluru
items.gist: The South Western Railway conducted a runtime trial of a 16-car Vande Bharat Express rake between Yeshwantpur and Mangaluru Central on Saturday, September 5, ahead of a proposed regular service linking Bengaluru and coastal Karnataka. The 2023-make rake, fitted with automatic emergency braking, became the first train-set to run on electric traction end-to-end on the sector, though it reached Mangaluru at 4.25 p.m.

items.headline: Thousands take part in Vittlapindi celebrations
items.gist: Udupi's grand Vittlapindi celebrations on Saturday were inaugurated by Krishnapura Mutt seer Sri Vidyasagara Theertha Swamiji and featured a wrestling bout in front of Shiroor Mutt, dancing tigers, Marakalu performers and the Mosaru Kudike ritual of breaking pots filled with curds and milk. A clay idol of Lord Krishna was taken in a golden palanquin procession through Car Street, with thousands watching tiger dance groups, a traditional slippery areca nut tree competition and children dressed as little Krishnas before the idol was taken to Madhwa Sarovar for immersion.

items.gist: Dakshina Kannada District in-charge Minister U.T. Khader inaugurated the district-level Praja Seva meeting in Puttur on Saturday, saying the government has established the Department of Praja Seva to hear and redress the grievances of every citizen and deliver the benefits of every government scheme.
items.paragraph: Dakshina Kannada District in-charge Minister U.T. Khader inaugurated the district-level Praja Seva meeting in Puttur on Saturday, saying the government has established the Department of Praja Seva to hear and redress the grievances of every citizen and deliver the benefits of every government scheme. On the inaugural day, a total of 163 applications were received from the public, including 61 for Revenue, 22 for Rural Development and 13 for Police; complaints covered land sanction, plotting, title deeds, survey, gun licences, bus sanctions and provision of teachers for schools. Mr. Khader distributed title deeds to beneficiaries and said issues pending for 20 to 30 years have been resolved; Puttur MLA Ashok Kumar Rai and district-level officials were present.

items.headline: 'Teachers play crucial role in guiding society'
items.gist: Udupi-Chikmagalur MP Kota Srinivasa Poojary, inaugurating district-level Teachers' Day celebrations in Udupi on Saturday to mark Dr Sarvepalli Radhakrishnan's birth anniversary, said teachers guide society from ignorance towards knowledge and have a great responsibility as primary education lays the foundation for a child's future. He said teachers are mentors who instil patriotism and encourage children to discover their talents, and urged them to discharge their duties with dedication as children often emulate their lifestyles and ideas.

items.headline: Shakti scheme: Free smart cards for 1 cr women soon
items.gist: Transport Minister Byrathi Suresh said on Friday that free smart cards will soon be issued to more than one crore women bus passengers under the Shakti scheme for Rs 250 crore, as the first phase of a project that will eventually cover more than three crore women. The government is introducing the cards to weed out leakages — such as conductors issuing tickets to inflate numbers — and to streamline expenditure amid pressure on city bus conductors to issue tickets quickly.
items.paragraph: Transport Minister Byrathi Suresh said on Friday that free smart cards will soon be issued to more than one crore women bus passengers under the Shakti scheme for Rs 250 crore, as the first phase of a project that will eventually cover more than three crore women. The government is introducing the cards to weed out leakages — such as conductors issuing tickets to inflate numbers — and to streamline expenditure amid pressure on city bus conductors to issue tickets quickly. The smart cards will function like bank cards readable by Electronic Ticketing Machines, storing beneficiary photos, domicile details, boarding and alighting points, distance travelled and fare, allowing beneficiaries to tap the card on the ETM instead of presenting ID.

items.headline: Yellappa Reddy offers to work with govt on tunnel road fix
items.gist: Veteran environmentalist A N Yellappa Reddy, who had launched a physical petition and signature campaign against the Act that allowed diversion of park land, has written to Chief Minister D K Shivakumar offering to support the government to figure out alternatives to the Tunnel Road after the Cabinet on Thursday decided to withdraw the contentious Karnataka Government Parks (Preservation) (Amendment) Act, 2026. items.headline: 'Classrooms have turned into caste-rooms': Activists decry suppression of dissent
items.gist: Marking the 10th anniversary of Gauri Lankesh's assassination, AISA Karnataka organised a panel titled "Campuses to Streets: Is Democracy Under Siege?" in Bengaluru on Saturday, launching a booklet on public education with a Karnataka focus. Speakers including JNUSU joint secretary Danish Ali, sociologist Prof Lakshmipathi C G and poet-activist Meena Kandasamy linked Lankesh's 2017 killing to ongoing suppression of dissent, caste hierarchies in education, self-censorship, NEP commercialisation and India's 157th rank on the World Press Freedom Index, calling for campus activism to join broader democratic movements.

items.headline: Bengaluru-Delhi container train service launched
items.gist: Union Minister of State for Railways and Jal Shakti V Somanna flagged off a weekly CONCOR-operated container train on Saturday linking Bengaluru's Whitefield ICD to Tughlakabad in Delhi via Tondiarpet in Chennai, with a 166-hour transit window for CONCOR-owned domestic cargo. items.headline: 'One Nation, One Education' dismantles secular values, pluralism: Hariprasad
items.gist: KPCC chief B K Hariprasad on Saturday attacked the Centre's NEP 2020 and Prime Minister Narendra Modi at a Teachers' Day event in Bengaluru, alleging they are systematically eroding India's secular foundation and that 'One Nation, One Education' dismantles secular values. Contrasting Modi with former education ministers such as Maulana Abul Kalam Azad, V K R V Rao and P V Narasimha Rao, he recalled Gauri Lankesh's 2017 assassination and urged teachers to safeguard constitutional values; education activist Dr V P Niranjanaradhya urged the Congress government to effectively implement the RTE Act, citing over 1.5 lakh government school closures or mergers between 2014 and 2024 and 2.26 crore students dropping out of government schools.

items.headline: 'Amid inflation, BPL income limit of Rs 1.2 lakh needs a hike'
items.gist: Food Minister Rizwan Arshad told DH the Anna Bhagya scheme now provides 7.5 kg rice plus 2.5 kg ragi or jowar instead of 10 kg rice, and that he cancelled the Indira kit tender to remodel it after studying the supply chain. items.headline: K'taka seeks sharp cut in quantum of water release to TN
items.gist: Karnataka has appealed to the Cauvery Water Management Authority to cut daily releases to Tamil Nadu from 9,000 cusec to 2,000 cusec at Biligundlu, citing storage of just 66.629 tmcft in four major reservoirs amid an unprecedented super El Niño. Additional chief secretary Gaurav Gupta said the state needs about 154 tmcft for irrigation, drinking water including Bengaluru and environmental flows, while Tamil Nadu's Mettur reservoir holds about 55 tmcft plus expected catchment contributions of about 100 tmcft, and objected to CWRC and CWMA orders in July and August without waiting for a post-monsoon distress assessment.

items.headline: 14 ancient gold coins discovered
items.gist: Four job card holders engaged in work under the VB-G RAM G scheme in Belagavi district found 14 ancient gold coins weighing 54.88 gm near BCM Hostel in Inchal village of Saundatti taluk on August 29 and promptly handed them to government authorities on Friday; the coins have been deposited in the treasury. items.gist: Two Zilla Panchayat engineers and Government Higher Primary School head master C B Helavar were suspended in Bagalkot district after a concrete ceiling portion collapsed at a school in Mugallolli Tanda; the DDPI suspended Helavar for allegedly failing to report the building's deteriorating condition, and ZP CEO Gajanan Bale suspended Assistant Executive Engineer S M Revadi and Junior Engineer S M Sanganal. items.headline: Govt vehicles violate traffic rules, pile up over 82k cases in 3 years
items.gist: Government vehicles in Karnataka accumulated over 82,000 traffic violations between 2023 and July 2026 with Rs 19.56 crore in unpaid penalties, Legislative Council data show, with only Rs 47.72 lakh recovered. Home Minister Priyank Kharge said individual drivers, not taxpayers, must pay fines under the Motor Vehicles Act, though the government has issued no specific protocol for recovering outstanding fines on official vehicles; Mysuru City recorded 28,708 non-police government-vehicle violations in 2024 and 35,870 in 2025.

items.headline: Fix glitches in Kaveri portal: HC to govt.
items.gist: The High Court of Karnataka has directed the State government to immediately rectify technical flaws in the Kaveri 2.0 registration portal that have halted property transactions under perpetual leaseholds in several parts of the State, particularly the Belagavi region, giving authorities two months to enable registration. Justice Sachin Shankar Magadum, allowing a petition by Belagavi-based builder Gopalrao Kukdolkar who could not register 13 of 34 flats because municipal records mapped the original lessor as “owner” rather than the Nirantara Patta leaseholder, held that a software mapping defect cannot restrict substantive property rights and that citizens should not be forced to approach the High Court individually because of a technological defect affecting an entire class of properties.

items.headline: RERA leaves homebuyers in lurch in battle against builders

items.headline: Strong law, weak delivery
items.gist: Despite RERA passing orders in favour of aggrieved homebuyers, advocates and industry experts say weak enforcement often leaves buyers in long legal battles through appellate tribunals and courts, while developers may use insolvency proceedings under the IBC to stall execution. Section 14 moratorium under the IBC holds statutory supremacy over RERA under Section 238, pausing recovery when NCLT admits an insolvency petition.

items.headline: Stalled projects: RERA's unfinished challenge
items.gist: The scale of India's stalled-project crisis highlights RERA's limits on ensuring timely completion: the Indian Banks' Association in 2023 estimated 4.12 lakh stressed housing units involving Rs 4.08 lakh crore, with an Amitabh Kant-led committee identifying lack of financial viability as the primary cause. Karnataka RERA data as of August 2026 shows 2,591 Revenue Recovery Certificates issued worth Rs 1,228.40 crore, but only 329 projects recovered Rs 123.84 crore while 2,262 worth Rs 1,104.56 crore remain pending.

items.headline: 2 die, 250 injured during Maha Janmashtami celebrations
items.gist: Two persons, including seven-year-old Rudra Kadam who died when a brick column collapsed during dahi handi in the Mumbai Metropolitan Region, and 45-year-old Salma Salauddin Pathan who died in Pune after a loudspeaker structure fell on her, were killed while more than 250 people were injured across Maharashtra during Krishna Janmashtami festivities on Saturday. BMC-run hospitals reported 118 injured revellers in Mumbai, with five admitted, and Deputy CM Eknath Shinde in Thane urged participants to prioritise safety over record-breaking human pyramids.

items.headline: Parandur airport axed, leaving villagers divided over land's future
items.gist: Residents of Ekanapuram, who protested the proposed Greenfield Airport at Parandur for nearly four years, are celebrating after Chief Minister C Joseph Vijay scrapped the project as promised in 2025, but villagers in 12 other Kanchipuram district villages where about 1,700 acres were acquired or marked for acquisition are divided over the TVK government plan to repurpose the land for non-polluting industries. While some compensated farmers welcome staying in their villages, others oppose nearby factories, question whether fragmented parcels can form an industrial estate, and demand that acquisition freezes be lifted so they can pledge or sell land after years of uncertainty since the August 24 cancellation announcement.

items.headline: Secunderabad arms theft was inside job: Investigators
items.gist: Five days after weapons went missing from the 20th Battalion of the Madras Regiment at Bollarum in Secunderabad Cantonment, investigators have not identified the perpetrators but concluded it was an insider job, with CCTV in the store room switched off and record books poorly maintained while suspicion focuses on four individuals. The theft reported on August 31 included five assault rifles such as AK-203 and INSAS models, seven pistols, magazines, ammunition and a night-vision device last accounted for on August 30, and a multi-agency probe involving military intelligence, Central agencies and Telangana Police is urgently seeking the missing arms before they reach anti-social elements.

items.headline: Terrorist killed in Budgam identified as Pakistani national
items.gist: The terrorist killed on Friday in operation 'Ashdar' in Budgam's Ashdar Gali area has been identified as Yasir, a Pakistani national and alleged Lashkar-e-Taiba member, Jammu and Kashmir Police said on Saturday. Security forces acting on specific inputs about movement in the Pir Panjal belt challenged the suspects, who opened fire; troops retaliated and recovered an AK-series rifle and other war-like stores, in the Kashmir Valley's second confirmed encounter this year after Shopian on July 8.

items.headline: 'Charge of compromising position doesn't prove adultery'
items.gist: The Patna High Court held that merely alleging a spouse was seen in a compromising position with another person is insufficient to prove adultery as a ground for divorce under the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955. A division bench of Justices Bibek Chaudhuri and Rana Vikram Singh on Thursday dismissed a man's appeal after he claimed his wife had an illicit relationship with her brother-in-law and deserted him since March 13, 2013, upholding the family court's refusal to grant divorce on adultery and cruelty grounds.

items.headline: Narendran leads Tata Sons succession race
items.gist: Tata Sons has narrowed its search for a successor to Chairman N Chandrasekaran—who will not seek reappointment when his second five-year term ends on February 20, 2027—to Tata Steel CEO and MD T V Narendran, Tata Sons executive director and group CFO Saurabh Agrawal, and NSE MD and CEO Ashish Chauhan, with Narendran seen as the frontrunner among internal candidates. Sources said Tata Trusts chairman Noel Tata has flagged the shortlist to top government leaders, though the board and controlling trusts have made no official confirmation and other names such as Noel Tata, Aarthi Subramanian, Shailesh Chandra and Praveer Sinha have also surfaced.

items.headline: NIA court convicts 10 Maoists in 2013 Jheeram Valley massacre case
items.gist: A Special NIA Court in Chhattisgarh's Jagdalpur has convicted ten Maoists in the 2013 Jheeram Valley massacre in Sukma, in which at least 27 people including top Congress leaders were killed in a Naxal attack on May 25, 2013 when Maoists attacked a convoy of Congress leaders around 10 km from Darbha police station returning from a Parivartan Yatra rally. items.headline: Census advanced in four poll-bound States, formally deferred in Manipur
items.gist: The Union government on Saturday advanced the Population Enumeration phase of Census 2027 in poll-bound Uttar Pradesh, Punjab, Uttarakhand and Goa, scheduling the exercise from November 16, 2026, to January 4, 2027, ahead of the nationwide enumeration planned for February 2027, and formally deferred the Census exercise in Manipur till further declaration. The second phase will have 40 questions including an open-ended field for caste details, with respondents able to not disclose caste or state they belong to none; at least 13 new questions compared with 2011 cover spouse's name, nationality, parents' particulars, digital literacy, permanent address, Covid-19 vaccination, bank accounts, passport, driving licence, mobile, Aadhaar and voter ID.

items.headline: Elephanta's maritime past comes into focus
items.gist: Indian scientists led by IIT Kharagpur will probe how past climate and sea-level changes shaped maritime trade around Elephanta island after archaeological digs recovered Roman and West Asian artefacts, anchoring stones and a 165 sq m ancient stepwell, suggesting the Unesco site was once a major port despite today's shallow waters limiting boats. The post-monsoon drilling at Elephanta, Nala Sopara and other Konkan sites will use radiocarbon dating of sediment cores to reconstruct roughly five-metre sea-level fluctuations over 5,000 years and Elephanta's role in wider maritime circuits.

items.headline: RERA under the judicial lens
items.gist: Chief Justice of India Surya Kant said in February 2026 that states should think of the people for whom RERA was created, adding that except facilitating builders in default it was "not doing anything else" and that abolishing the institution would be acceptable. A Supreme Court division bench comprising Justices Surya Kant and Ujjal Bhuyan said in September 2024 that RERA had become "rehabilitation centers for former bureaucrats who have frustrated the entire scheme of the Act."

items.headline: Where RERA falls short
items.gist: State-driven implementation has produced uneven efficiency, with nearly 75% of state RERAs failing to publish or update annual reports per the Forum for People's Collective Efforts; many refund and interest orders remain unexecuted, authorities face backlogs with limited staff, punitive action such as blacklisting or imprisonment has been rare, and multi-tiered appeals undermine speedy resolution.

items.headline: Keralam cleric's remark triggers rare political backlash
items.gist: A Samastha circular and remarks by 95-year-old Grand Mufti of India A P Aboobacker Musliyar of Kanthapuram—discouraging public display of women and mixing un-Islamic customs with Islamic celebrations amid Mawlid al-Nabi events overlapping Onam—have sparked a rare political backlash in Keralam, with Chief Minister V D Satheesan and all mainstream parties except IUML condemning the stance. Satheesan cited Khadija and Aisha from Islamic history to rebut the scholar, while Kanthapuram's supporters noted his record on women's education and charity even as CPM leaders compared his comments to RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat's 2013 remarks and the BJP questioned Rahul Gandhi's silence.

items.headline: Voter lists shrink over 15% since 2024 elections in States, U.T.s where SIR third-phase draft lists are out
items.gist: Since the 2024 Lok Sabha elections, voter lists of 17 States and Union Territories where Special Intensive Revision (SIR) is under way in its third phase have shrunk by 15.7% as per draft rolls published by the Election Commission, from 35,50,50,008 to 29,93,00,115. Maharashtra recorded the largest drop in absolute numbers, losing 15,896,198 electors or 17.08% in the draft phase, while Delhi and Chandigarh registered the sharpest dips in percentage at 35.89% and 31.84% respectively.

items.gist: A three-member team from the National Investigation Agency visited the crime scene at Bolaram’s Madras Regiment in Secunderabad on Friday and met investigators probing the disappearance of arms and detonators from the premises. Four AK-203 assault rifles, an INSAS 1B1 rifle, six 9 mm Auto 1A pistols, a civilian 6.35-bore pistol and more than 1,800 rounds of ammunition were reported missing from the Army premises, and a field-level officer said the investigation had been divided among personnel and teams with specific tasks.

items.headline: World-class education key to Viksit Bharat: President
items.gist: President Droupadi Murmu conferred National Awards on teachers from across the country at a function in New Delhi on September 5, commemorated as Teachers' Day, saying education is the most effective means of realising the ideal of equality of opportunity enshrined in the Constitution. She said a negligible primary school dropout rate had been made possible through teachers' efforts, that school education forms the foundation of the system, and that teaching good conduct in childhood is far more effective than acquiring knowledge and skills later.

items.gist: Prime Minister Narendra Modi stressed the need to address children's excessive screen time through sports and creative activities during a meeting with 82 National Award-winning teachers at his official residence on Friday. items.headline: Congress slams Centre over 'broken education system' on Teachers' Day
items.gist: The top Congress leadership used National Teachers' Day, commemorating former President Sarvepalli Radhakrishnan's birth anniversary, to highlight what they described as the "broken education system" under the Narendra Modi government. Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge posted a video presentation arguing that the education sector had all but collapsed in the past 12 years, citing an alleged 80% jump in student suicides and 1.23 lakh student suicides during this period, 94,000 schools shut, 2.26 crore children wiped out of enrolment, government school share down from 71% to 49%, and four out of every 10 children dropping out by Class 12.

items.headline: SC directs Union Home Secretary to file affidavit on IPS postings in CAPFs
items.gist: The Supreme Court's order in the Central Armed Police Forces cadre case, uploaded on Saturday, asked Union Home Secretary Govind Mohan to explain the procedure followed for bringing IPS officers on deputation to the CAPFs, whether borrowing organisations made formal requisitions, and the reasons for such appointments despite the court's May 23, 2025 direction to progressively reduce IPS deputation posts up to the Senior Administrative Grade level. On September 2, while hearing a contempt petition, Justice Ujjal Bhuyan had orally observed there was a "strong lobby" and CAPF cadre officers were completely stifled; the Home Secretary's affidavit said 46 IPS officers have been brought on deputation to the CAPFs up to the SAG level after the 2025 judgment, including 13 to BSF, 11 to CISF, nine to CRPF, six to ITBP and seven to SSB.

items.headline: Centre obstructing caste census to prevent true representation: Thakare
items.gist: All India Congress Committee in-charge for Goa, Daman & Diu, and Dadra & Nagar Haveli Manikrao Thakare on Saturday claimed the NDA government at the Centre is deliberately obstructing a caste census to prevent "true representation" of Other Backward Classes and Extremely Backward Classes. items.headline: Climate scientist Krishna AchutaRao passes away
items.gist: Krishna AchutaRao, a leading voice in climate and atmospheric sciences and professor at the Centre for Atmospheric Sciences, IIT Delhi, died on Friday at 62. Among his key contributions was determining the degree to which observed climatic change could be attributed to human activity, with collaborative work demonstrating detectable human influence on temperature changes across Indian sub-regions; over two decades at IIT Delhi he served as Head of the Centre for Atmospheric Sciences and Dean (Faculty), helped establish the Centre of Excellence for Climate Change Adaptation, and worked at Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory before returning to India in 2007.

items.headline: Probe on into 'counterfeit' rabies vaccine, says CDSCO
items.gist: The Central Drugs Laboratory in Kasauli, Himachal Pradesh, has flagged a batch of Abhayrab vaccine used against rabies as "not of standard quality" and "misbranded" after it failed a potency test, raising concerns of counterfeit circulation and prompting a probe. items.headline: Former wrestler, two children found dead in Maharashtra fort
items.gist: Former national-level wrestler Ashwini Pol, 30, and her two children have been found dead in a 100-foot gorge at the Naldurg fort in Maharashtra's Dharashiv district; her third child, found seriously injured at the site, is on ventilator support. items.headline: Why is BRICS exploring cross-border payments?
items.gist: Ahead of the 18th BRICS summit in New Delhi in September, finance ministries and central bank representatives met in Jaipur on August 12–13 to discuss linking digital payment systems and central bank digital currencies to cut cross-border costs that currently route through correspondent banks and SWIFT with repeated currency conversions. BRICS is exploring direct links between national payment systems—India and Singapore already linked UPI and PayNow—and shared hubs such as Project Nexus and CBDC platforms like mBridge, while India has proposed linking members’ CBDCs for trade and tourism while framing the effort as cost reduction rather than displacing the dollar.

items.headline: What are totalisers and how do they prevent candidates from determining the voting pattern of individual polling booths?
items.gist: On September 1, a Supreme Court Bench headed by Chief Justice Surya Kant asked the Centre to examine introducing totaliser machines that consolidate votes from about 14 EVMs without revealing booth-wise patterns, in a 2014 PIL by Yogesh Gupta and Imran Khan seeking to prevent voter intimidation. The Centre has consistently opposed totalisers, arguing booth-wise results help candidates improve outreach and warning of data-breach risks, while the Election Commission has supported the measure since first recommending it in 2008; the Court has asked both the government and the poll panel to state their positions on impediments and impacts.

items.headline: Glacial collapse unlikely to halt China's dam plan
items.gist: China has already opened the Zangmu dam on the middle reaches of the Yarlung Zangbo, which a state media report said had provided a solution to nearly 26% of electricity demand in Southwest China's Xizang (Tibet) Autonomous Region and included an elaborate fishway for future projects. In June, a final acceptance meeting declared the dam, which started construction in 2010, had generated 22.2 billion kilowatt-hours of energy.
items.paragraph: China has already opened the Zangmu dam on the middle reaches of the Yarlung Zangbo, which a state media report said had provided a solution to nearly 26% of electricity demand in Southwest China's Xizang (Tibet) Autonomous Region and included an elaborate fishway for future projects. In June, a final acceptance meeting declared the dam, which started construction in 2010, had generated 22.2 billion kilowatt-hours of energy. The new project near the India border at the "great bend" is expected to dwarf Zangmu, with Chinese analysts projecting 60 GW installed capacity and 300 billion kilowatt-hours of power a year; though described as run-of-the-river, it will involve a reservoir likely at Mainling, with water diverted through an approximately 40-km tunnel to five 12-GW powerhouses. India and China will hold an Expert-Level Mechanism on Transborder Rivers meeting later this month, though hydrological data sharing has not been regular; China's Foreign Ministry spokesperson Guo Jiakun said Beijing maintains a highly responsible attitude and that the project is beneficial for disaster prevention without adverse downstream effects.

items.headline: ISL Season 13 to begin on October 10
items.gist: The 13th season of the Indian Super League will begin on October 10 under a new club-led structure, returning to a traditional home-and-away format with 13 teams and 163 matches over seven months until May 2027. The table-topper after the double-leg league will be crowned Shield winner and official champion, while the top six will compete in playoffs for the ISL Cup; Diamond Harbour FC will not take its promoted slot after failing to meet the administrative fee, and Churchill Brothers FC entered after acquiring Jamshedpur FC’s licence.

items.headline: When pets become premium customers, get insurance cover
items.gist: Pet owners in India are increasingly paying premiums for high-end products and specialised veterinary care, with brands such as Royal Canin becoming common and treatments like haemodialysis and laparoscopic surgery in demand. Pet insurance is gradually gaining attention—Bajaj Allianz entered the market in 2021 and premiums can start at ₹1,700 annually—but remains unfamiliar to the wider public, hampered by lack of documentation at veterinary hospitals and slow cashless claim reimbursements; IMARC projects India’s pet insurance market to grow from $331.1 million in 2025 to an estimated $993.4 million by 2034.

items.headline: Odd expressions
items.gist: People often make tense facial expressions when self-administering eye drops because placing a drop requires controlling fine movement while something approaches a sensitive part of the face, activating muscles beyond those strictly needed. The blink reflex when the dropper nears the eye adds further tension around the eyes, forehead and mouth as the person suppresses blinking while keeping the eye open and aiming accurately.

items.gist: Researchers have developed a way to detect Zika and hepatitis C viruses in whole blood using a new blood-drying protocol that traps and shields RNA with only a heater and a low-cost sensor. The method finds the viruses in two hours with accuracy comparable to top labs, avoiding the pricey equipment normally needed to purify blood samples before RNA testing.

items.headline: Scans reveal how brain allows humans to speak silently
items.gist: Using magnetoencephalography, scientists found that during inner speech the brain’s motor regions first encode how the mouth should move for a sound, after which auditory regions activate to represent the predicted sound of syllables. The brain organised vowels based on acoustic properties even though no sound was made, suggesting inner speech is a motor simulation rather than just abstract thought.

items.headline: The infrastructure, talent and market challenges of catching up late
items.gist: India's 1976 Semiconductor Complex Limited in Mohali was manufacturing 5,000-nm chips by 1984 before a 1989 fire and bureaucratic delays stalled momentum, making today's multi-billion-dollar subsidies the price of lost silicon sovereignty. A 2023 assessment found imports account for about 85% of initial fab setup costs; Tata-PSMC's $11 billion Dholera venture and Micron's $2.75 billion Sanand ATMP facility highlight infrastructure and execution hurdles, while Deloitte says India must train four to five lakh semiconductor professionals annually and NITI Aayog warns of a design-versus-manufacturing skills gap.

items.headline: Is India overpaying for its semiconductor dream?
items.gist: India's Semicon 2.0 adds Rs 1,27,500 crore ($13.3 billion) to an initial Rs 76,000 crore mission, offering up to 50% capital subsidies for fabs as New Delhi tries to catch up in the global chip race against the US CHIPS Act's $52.7 billion and Europe's €43 billion Chips Act. items.headline: Ten-sided wave undulates around Saturn’s south pole
items.gist: Scientists have for the first time found a decagonal wave around Saturn’s south pole, using images from space and ground telescopes in 2023–2025. The wave moves slowly eastward, with its vertices shifting back and forth every 32 days; researchers believe it is a vertical atmospheric structure that may have formed due to unstable winds or a nearby anticyclone.

items.headline: Striped hyenas help keep India clean, but remain misunderstood (Opinion)
items.gist: Estimates suggest 5,000–14,000 striped hyenas exist worldwide, with 1,000–3,000 in India, yet India lacks an official census and folklore associating hyenas with witches hampers conservation despite the highest legal protection under the Wildlife (Protection) Act 1972. items.headline: What is ‘One Nation, One Time’?
items.gist: On August 27, the Centre notified the Legal Metrology (Indian Standard Time) Rules, 2026, making Indian Standard Time the single reference for legal, administrative, commercial and official purposes, with the Rules taking effect 180 days after Gazette publication to allow systems to adapt. IST, maintained by CSIR-NPL with a UTC +5:30 offset and disseminated with millisecond accuracy, will support banking, digital payments, telecom, railways, power networks and government records; the Rules emphasise NavIC and other approved Indian timing sources to reduce dependence on foreign satellite-based time such as GPS, including a White Rabbit Technology-based IST dissemination pilot commissioned in Bengaluru in July 2026.
